directive.quote: Move the account protocol behind the engine. The shell keeps only: start, liveness, restart, show the page, and one opaque secret store.

sources.what: reconcileWithLocalRuntime: the shell asking the engine for the app's key on each page
acceptAccountAnswer: key same, a new key revealed, the device key
adoptPendingKey: keep the issued key in the Keychain item
resourceKeyFromAnswer, adoptResourceKey, forgetResourceKey: the device key kept and handed to the connection
keptKey, keep, forgetKey, keychain: the Keychain item read and written through /usr/bin/security

targets.what: keep_app_key and KeptSecrets: one check of the app's key
with_app_key: the pass at start and every recheck_seconds beside the outbound connection, over the blob the app sent back
parent_loop: after the launch message the parent's stdin carries host events only; the shell's old account request and device-key control messages are let go, never answered
ParentKept: the app's opaque kept blob from the launch message, each change handed back in one keep message; owner_door: the launch's owner binding admitted at the door as the key held here
the launch message's owner_binding and kept, the keep message and the shared private stdout (ParentWriter)
SecretsKey::kept_before: the secrets key (vault root) this computer kept before the app kept it, only read; SecretsKeySource::HostingApp opens the vault with the root the app sent back
SecretsKeySource::HostingApp, give and given: the root the hosting app keeps, given once at launch

preserve: a key the account's sign-in still admits is kept as it is (key same)
a key the sign-in does not admit, or none kept, is replaced by one the sign-in issues, kept by the app in its one store (handed over in a keep message, sent back at the next launch)
the device key the engine enrolls is kept beside it and given to the outbound connection with the same waits (1000, 5000, 60000 ms; 1 s connect; 5 s io)
a store that does not answer is not an empty store: no key is issued on a failed read
secrets never reach argv, a file, or a log
allowed_deltas: the engine, not the shell, asks and keeps: once at start and every recheck_seconds (DATA), instead of on each page load
an issued key the home refuses is held in memory and asked with next, instead of being dropped
the shell's forget-on-sign-out is not ported: the native path never answered signed_out

not ported, the same fault in a build that carries no engine: the sandboxed (Mac App Store) build still asks the hosted page for its key and keeps it in its own Keychain item, at the sources' repository commit b56775468a macos/App/ComputerReader.swift lines 170-286 (keyFromPage), 1069-1090 (resourceKeyFromAnswer, adoptResourceKey, forgetResourceKey) and 1312-1322 (keep, forgetKey), each behind Self.sandboxed; that build does not ship, and its key needs a hosted keeper before it can follow this port

the engine's half of the old shell protocol is removed, not kept beside the port: the account request and its signed result, the launch message's device key and the parent's device-key control (src/native.rs, src/native_host.rs, src/account.rs), and the older native-serve STATE ADDRESS argv (src/main.rs, src/native_entry.rs run). The shell and the engine ship in one app, and the shell stopped sending them at the sources' repository commit b56775468a; a message that still arrives is let go unanswered. Same case, 2026-11-03

the engine keeps no secret itself: it decides the app's key and device key and hands them to the app that launched it as one opaque blob in a keep message on its private stdout; the app stores the blob in its one store and sends it back as the next launch message's kept. No Keychain item or secret file is written by the engine, so an engine run on a copied state or a made-up account can only hand its blob to its own parent (this replaces the descriptor-provenance fence and the per-state Keychain items of the previous commit). Team lead, case source:YmxvY2tlci0yLXNoZWxsLWVuZ2luZS1hY2NvdW50LXNwbGl0LTIwMjYtMTEtMDMtMDUyNy1tc3Q option (a): the engine never writes the Mac Keychain, 2026-11-03

the app's own calls at the door carry the launch's owner binding instead of the key: the door admits that bearer as the key held now (owner_door); the app never holds a key it can read. Same case, 2026-11-03

the vault root is kept by the app in the same blob: the engine opens the vault with the root the app sent back; when it sends none, the root this computer kept before (the secrets key's own item, or the old app key item it was first split from) is read once, never written, and handed to the app, and a computer that kept none gets a new root. A root the app sent that is not a root stops the start rather than setting the account's sealed values aside. replace_keychain_secrets_key, which nothing called, is removed. Operator commands outside the app (secrets, namespace) still open the vault through the root's own Keychain item (AccountRoot::from_keychain), the one engine path that may write it, on its first split only. Same case, 2026-11-03

the app opens its page through the engine: native::OWNER_PAGE_PATH with the launch's owner binding as the bearer answers 303 to the named page path with the workspace's own session cookie, read from the engine's own state (account_source ProtectedBrowserSession::token), instead of the app reading restore-receipt.json and browser-session.key and setting the cookie itself (the sources' repository macos/App/LocalWorkspaceBrowserSession.swift lines 155-170 at 959a5e996a). Same case, 2026-11-03

ported onto main 2026-11-05 (trillion-rust side/engine-keeps-nothing 2c742058, 5b3689b0, 542df2ce, 17effaa7, which share no history with main): held_values is src/secrets.rs and its root the secrets key (SecretsKey, SecretsKeySource::HostingApp); the key kept before is looked for only where the launcher's product settings declare a Keychain secret home (identity.json section secret_home), else none was kept; the window cookie is workspace_session WINDOW_COOKIE; the credential home is src/secrets/credential-home.json app_key_keeper
banned_substitutions: the engine writing a Keychain item or a secret file for the app's keys
the app reading or deciding inside the kept blob
issuing a key when the store could not be read
the owner binding in argv, the environment, a log or a message the engine writes

baseline.note: behavioural port from Swift to Rust; the old copy left the shell at the sources' repository commit b56775468a (blocker 2 shell step), apart from the sandboxed build's own path named in allowed_deltas
